children: U.S. stocks rebounded sharply Thursday, erasing two sessions of losses as crude oil retreated from its geopolitical spike and Treasury yields eased back below 5%, one day after the Federal Reserve delivered its first interest
The S&P 500 rose 1.1% to 7,635.21, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average lagged with a 0.7% advance, up 365 points to 51,827.04.
West Texas Intermediate fell 1.6% to $100.81 a barrel
Brent dropped 2.5% to $103.23, a one-week low

and a unanimous FOMC lifted the fed funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4% on Wednesday and projected at least one further increase this year, citing inflation that remains too high at 3.4% and a labor market at effectively full employment.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.95%, down 8 basis points and back under the 5.04% level hit earlier this week, which had marked a 19-year high.
The policy-sensitive 2-year yield slipped 6 basis points to 4.69%, while the 30-year eased 7 basis points to 5.30%.
The CBOE Volatility Index slid 11.4% to 15.69, unwinding the fear premium built up around the Fed decision and the Middle East supply scare.
Gold was the standout in commodities, jumping 2.5% to $4,368.71 an ounce as real yields retreated, with silver surging 4.1% to $65.86.

On the macro front, initial jobless claims fell 10,000 to 196,000, well below the 206,500 consensus and close to July’s 60-year low, while the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index slowed to 37.8 from 47.4 but comfortably beat the 32.1 estimate.
